subject: Proposal: Tri-region Minimal Viable Dedicated Footprint + Safety Buffers
messages:
From: Samuel King <samuel.king@orion.ai>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask for tri-region dedicated pools

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Orion is excited about moving from trial to a committed Dedicated footprint. We're working on a rollout plan across US, EU, and APAC and need a recommended minimal starting configuration (we'll call it the MVP footprint) plus a safety buffer for predictable bursts. High-level numbers from our side:
- Expected steady-state inference: ~120k tokens/sec global, skewed to US (55%), EU (30%), APAC (15%)
- Peak bursts up to 4x sustained for short windows (5–15m) during batch jobs and product launches
- Preferred model family: open-llama-v2-13b quantized (your profiling team suggested this as cost-effective)
- Hard constraints: data residency for EU (no cross-border caching) and a 99.95% latency SLO for US calls

Can you provide a short proposal that lays out:
1) minimal GPU counts per region for MVP + recommended safety buffer (percentage or nodes)
2) lead times and any procurement/commitment asks (tranches ok)
3) rough estimate of monthly committed cost (ballpark)

Procurement and legal will want an initial view for internal approval. CC'ing Karthik since he'll own the infra sizing follow-up.

Thanks,
Samuel
Samuel King
Head of Platforms, Orion.ai
procurement@orion.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, Samuel King <samuel.king@orion.ai>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sizing ask for tri-region dedicated pools — draft numbers

Folks — drafted a first-pass MVP footprint based on Orion's token/split and model family. Notes included inline in the sheet; summary below. Assumptions: 13B quantized model, average request length ~250 tokens, KV cache effective for repeated contexts, batching latency target <= 100ms p95.

Summary (MVP)
- US (55% traffic): 12x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (sustained), safety buffer +50% => 18 GPUs for burst headroom
- EU (30%): 6x A100-80GB equiv sustained, safety buffer +50% => 9 GPUs
- APAC (15%): 3x A100-80GB equiv sustained, safety buffer +67% => 5 GPUs (higher buffer due to region fragility and lead times)

Why this split: steady-state inferred from token velocity; we size for steady WP concurrency with continuous batching and enable automatic burst pools by reserving a small dedicated buffer and allowing cross-region fallback only for non-EU traffic.

Lead times & procurement notes:
- US/EU: 3–5 week lead for dedicated pool provisioning (infra ready for reservation + routing updates)
- APAC (Singapore): 6–10 week lead time depending on instance type availability and partner racks; recommend earlier commit or using a managed-hosted burst until dedicated nodes come online

Estimated committed cost (ballpark monthly):
- US (18 GPUs avg during burst) — $58k/mo
- EU (9 GPUs) — $29k/mo
- APAC (5 GPUs) — $18k/mo
Total ballpark committed run-rate: ~$105k/mo (depending on effective utilization, quantization, and batching gains)

Attachments: tri-region-sizing.xlsx (with per-GPU token capacity, concurrency assumptions, and cost math).

Open issues for commercial input:
- Desired commitment term (12/24/36) affects pricing and availability guarantees
- Appetite for initial hybrid approach (reserved steady-state + hosted-burst) to mitigate APAC lead times

-Karthik
Principal Infra PM, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Samuel King <samuel.king@orion.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 05:48:00 +0800
Subject: RE: Sizing ask for tri-region dedicated pools — APAC considerations

Hi team — quick APAC operational check:

1) Singapore provisioning: lead times vary by GPU type and partner. For A100-80GB equivalents we should budget 8 weeks to be conservative; if Orion is flexible with quantization profile we can reduce to ~6 weeks.
2) Minimum reservation granularity: some partners require a 4-GPU allocation as smallest block in APAC — that drives the higher safety multiplier for MVD.
3) Networking: for EU data-residency requirement we must not rely on cross-region cache; that increases per-region steady-state requirements.

Recommendation: staged delivery —
- Stage 0 (0–6 weeks): reserve US + EU minimal steady-state, route APAC traffic to Redwood-hosted burst pool (metered) to avoid procurement delays
- Stage 1 (6–12 weeks): spin up APAC dedicated nodes once partner confirms 4-GPU blocks; convert hosted-burst to dedicated buffer

I'll update the MOP doc (mvp-deployment-mop.pdf) with operational runbooks for failover and cache behavior.

-Hannah
Regional Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mvp-deployment-mop.pdf (doc stub)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.com, Samuel King <samuel.king@orion.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Tri-region Minimal Viable Dedicated Footprint + Safety Buffers — commercial view

Samuel — quick commercial framing to speed procurement:

Offer structure (recommended):
- Commit (12 months): baseline steady-state capacity with monthly billing and quarterly reconciliation for burst consumption
- Tranche 1 (MVP): US 12 GPUs, EU 6 GPUs size, APAC hosted-burst only — ramp to dedicated per Stage 1
- Tranche 2 (30 days after Stage 0): shift to full dedicated APAC 4 GPUs (minimum) and increase buffers as required

Discounting: 8–12% off list for a 12-month commit at the proposed baseline; a 15%+ discount tier for 24+ month commitments.

Key deliverables to include with the proposal: pricing table (monthly committed vs. burst), SLA addendum for dedicated pools, and a simple mutual action plan with dates. I can put this into a short PO-friendly PDF if you confirm the MVP numbers.

-Lauren
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
